title: Glassy Salted Peanut Brittle
summary: A hard, glassy peanut brittle of deep golden caramel and lots of warm roasted peanuts, made without butter so it is dairy-free.
equipment: heavy frying pan or wide saucepan (about 26 cm)

ingredients.item: neutral oil, for the tray and spatula
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Prepare the tray and nuts
steps.text: Heat the oven to 150 °C. Oil the tray, line it with baking paper and oil the paper and the spatula. Warm the peanuts in the oven for 8 min on a second tray or ovenproof plate.

steps.title: Dissolve the sugar
steps.text: Put the sugar and water in the pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar is evenly wet and starting to dissolve. Then stop stirring.

steps.title: Cook the caramel
steps.text: Let it bubble steadily for 8-12 min, swirling the pan now and then so it colours evenly, until it is a deep golden brown, about 170 °C. The colour can change quickly at the end, so stay close.

steps.title: Stir in the nuts
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, add the warm peanuts and salt, and stir quickly until every nut is coated in caramel.

steps.title: Spread out
steps.text: Pour onto the oiled paper immediately and press it into a thin layer with the oiled spatula before it begins to set.

steps.title: Cool and break
steps.text: Leave for 30-40 min until hard and glassy, then break into pieces.

tips: A common mistake is adding cold peanuts; they chill the caramel so it seizes into lumps before you can spread it.
If sugar crystals form on the side of the pan, brush them down with a pastry brush dipped in water.
Stop at deep golden; a shade darker and the caramel tastes bitter.
Use the same method with almonds or cashews; the nuts must be roasted and warm.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 weeks.
